az-ag-2026-mayes-kris.name: Kris Mayes
az-ag-2026-mayes-kris.bio: Arizona Attorney General; former Arizona Corporation Commissioner, ASU professor and political reporter.

positions.stance: Partners with law enforcement on funding and resources, targeting drug cartel members, fentanyl trafficking and criminals who take advantage of children.
Fights corporate price gouging, including prosecuting corporate landlords for inflating housing costs and standing up to data centers driving up utility bills.
Prosecutes those who scam vulnerable Arizonans and created an Elder Affairs Unit to investigate abuse and scams against seniors.
Takes on mega-farms draining rural water, sues polluters, and pushes for more regulation to stop corporations depriving families and small farms of water.
Prosecutes sexual predators and demands that AI companies put up safeguards and be held accountable for sexually explicit AI-generated images of minors.

az-ag-2026-petersen-warren.name: Warren Petersen
az-ag-2026-petersen-warren.bio: Arizona State Senate President who has served in the Arizona Legislature since 2012; attorney and business owner.

positions.stance: Will enforce the law "as written—not based on politics or personal opinion" and fight attempts to undermine state laws.
Opposes federal overreach, unconstitutional mandates and burdensome regulations, and will continue that fight as Attorney General.
Will ensure laws are enforced, hold criminals accountable, protect crime victims' rights and support law enforcement officers.
Will continue fighting to protect opportunities for female athletes and ensure the law is upheld.
Will use "every legal tool available" to defend rights from the Second Amendment to free speech.

az-treas-2026-norton-elijah.name: Elijah Norton
az-treas-2026-norton-elijah.bio: Businessman who founded and leads a group of companies employing more than 400 people.

positions.stance: Wants to work with the legislature on a first-of-its-kind audit of the entire state budget to cut fraud and return money to Arizonans.
Arizona's investments should go to companies that make a profit, not ones engaged in political or racial activism "of any type."
Will be a strong supporter of the Jewish community, opposes discrimination of any kind, and will ensure Arizona's investments reflect that.
Will expand access to Arizona's 529 education savings plan and advocate for school choice and education freedom.
Will call out politicians in either party who waste taxpayer dollars and work to keep taxes low and investments secure.

az-treas-2026-mansour-nick.name: Nick Mansour
az-treas-2026-mansour-nick.bio: Entrepreneur who built a nursing school and former CEO.

positions.stance: Will manage state trust land and the education endowment to generate more classroom funding "without raising taxes" on families or businesses.
Will demand transparency and oversight in the Treasurer's Office and act to stop misuse of ESA voucher funds on non-educational purchases.
Will work with Arizona agencies to attract companies, create jobs and strengthen small businesses in a long-term, sustainable way.
Will keep extreme political agendas out of the Treasurer's Office and invest state funds safely and responsibly.

az-spi-2026-yee-kimberly.name: Kimberly Yee
az-spi-2026-yee-kimberly.bio: Arizona State Treasurer since 2018; former Arizona Senate Majority Leader and Senate Education Committee chair.

positions.stance: Says Arizona children deserve a State Superintendent "who will fight to protect their educational freedom."

az-spi-2026-leyba-ruiz-teresa.name: Teresa Leyba Ruiz
az-spi-2026-leyba-ruiz-teresa.bio: Educator with 35 years of experience and former President of Glendale Community College.

positions.stance: Will create an ESA spending dashboard, end automatic approval of ESA expenditures of $2,000 or less, and establish rigorous audit protocols.
Will meet with families in every county in her first year and open advisory committee positions to parents and students.
Will expand early learning such as universal pre-K, strengthen CTE and dual enrollment, and focus on math and literacy.
Will celebrate public schools' achievements, restore respect for teaching, and serve as "Advocate-in-Chief" for public schools.
Will advocate for increased public school funding and "rein in the universal ESA program."

az-mine-inspector-2026-presmyk-walter.name: Walter "Les" Presmyk
az-mine-inspector-2026-presmyk-walter.bio: Mining engineer with over 45 years of mining experience, including as Salt River Project's Principal Mining Engineer; former Gilbert Town Council member.

positions.stance: Will serve as an ambassador for the mining industry.
Seeks MSHA certification for the department's New Miner Training for underground miners, using the University of Arizona's San Xavier mine.
Will provide staff with additional educational opportunities for professional advancement.
Will continuously improve staff performance and actions.
Supports Arizona State University's Center for Mining Innovation.

az-mine-inspector-2026-matlock-brian.name: Brian Matlock
az-mine-inspector-2026-matlock-brian.bio: Marine veteran and mechanical engineer with decades of heavy-industry experience, including mining.

positions.stance: Lists worker safety and accident prevention as a priority: "It's not just about mining - it's about mining safely."
Lists abandoned mine hazards as a priority.
Lists strengthening relationships with rural and tribal communities as a priority.
Lists modernizing the Mine Inspector's Office as a priority.

az-corp-comm-2026-thompson-kevin.name: Kevin Thompson
az-corp-comm-2026-thompson-kevin.bio: Arizona Corporation Commissioner and Air Force veteran; former Mesa City Council member and Southwest Gas engineer.

positions.stance: Will continue fighting energy mandates and subsidies such as the REST and DSM/EE standards that he says shift costs to ratepayers.
Will keep fighting "Green New Deal and California-style energy policies" in Arizona.
Opposes shifting the costs of building and serving data centers and other large-load customers onto residential and small business ratepayers.
Ended ratepayer-funded subsidies to homebuilders for appliances in new homes, saying the savings were not passed on to homeowners.
Will work with utilities to proactively reduce water losses from leaking pipelines.

az-corp-comm-2026-hill-jonathon.name: Jonathon Hill
az-corp-comm-2026-hill-jonathon.bio: Scientist and engineer who has worked for 20 years at Arizona State University on NASA space missions.

positions.stance: Commits to restoring the Corporation Commission as "a fair, transparent body that prioritizes the people of Arizona over corporate interests."
Says data centers should no longer have their energy and water costs subsidized by Arizona residents.
Says the Commission should do more to protect the water supply and water access for lower-income Arizonans.
Will replace rushed, formula-based rate adjustments with full public hearings and community input before any rate increase.
Will demand strict scrutiny of utility spending so ratepayers do not subsidize mega-users like data centers.

az-corp-comm-2026-pratte-clara.name: Clara Pratte
az-corp-comm-2026-pratte-clara.bio: Co-founder of Navajo Power and small business owner; former senior official at the U.S. Small Business Administration and Department of Commerce.

positions.stance: Promises to fight for affordable residential utility bills and says lowering costs is her top priority.
Will demand transparency and accountability from utility companies.
Will ensure data centers pay their fair share.
Will protect Arizona's water resources.
Will advocate for rural and tribal communities and invest in Arizona's energy future.
Making life more affordable "by putting money directly back into people's pockets."
Defending freedoms "against Trump-era rollbacks that threaten our fundamental rights."
Fighting for the next generation and expanding opportunity for every child.
The Attorney General must uphold and enforce existing laws, including the legislative audit: "No selective enforcement. No political shielding."
Opposes state-imposed zoning mandates that override Home Rule and coerce municipalities under threat of funding loss.
The Attorney General should be independent, not an extension of the Legislature or a political arm of the Governor's Office.
Will fight utility rate hikes and hold utility companies accountable.
Will bring competence and rigor to vetting ballot questions so they are clear, lawful and honest.

ma-sos-2026-galvin-william.name: William Francis Galvin
ma-sos-2026-galvin-william.bio: Secretary of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

positions.stance: Is resisting in federal court federal efforts to limit Massachusetts citizens' voter registration, voting by mail, and voters' personal information.
Intends to expose and resist any federal interference with the popular vote and Electoral College process in 2028.
Wants an accurate and inclusive 2030 Census count, opposing efforts to limit counting of group quarters or exclude non-native-born residents.

ma-sos-2026-brensley-anne.name: Anne R. Brensley
ma-sos-2026-brensley-anne.bio: CEO of DevCo North America and former Wayland Selectwoman.

positions.stance: Will ensure secure ballot access, modernize election safeguards, and support town clerks with better tools and resources.
Will implement better verification tools to prevent fraud and strengthen safeguards against manipulation in the ballot process.
Will improve public records access and response times and embrace digital-first government services.
Will modernize the Corporations Division, simplify online LLC formation, and reduce unnecessary bureaucracy and compliance costs.
Will implement better technology and customer service systems and improve accessibility and processing times.
Supports investments in shovel-ready projects to address housing affordability.
Creating public-private partnerships to fund financial education and teacher training in schools.
Wants to expand the Baby Steps Savings Plan beyond its 53,000 enrolled families.
Holding corporations accountable on executive pay, insisting on climate risk mitigation, and ensuring employees are treated with dignity.
Providing resources for small business owners and supporting a program that deposits state cash in banks to expand small business lending.

ma-treas-2026-dionne-elizabeth.name: Elizabeth Dionne
ma-treas-2026-dionne-elizabeth.bio: Chair of the Belmont Select Board and former attorney at Boston law firms.

positions.stance: Will ensure every taxpayer dollar is spent wisely and efficiently.
Will "disinfect the State House by opening the books and reporting to you."
Will maximize returns on state pension funds and investments.
Will put the interests of taxpayers first, "not political agendas."

ma-aud-2026-dizoglio-diana.name: Diana DiZoglio
ma-aud-2026-dizoglio-diana.bio: Massachusetts State Auditor and former state senator.

positions.stance: Will analyze and report on state spending with minority-owned businesses and highlight areas needing improvement.
Will examine state contracts to ensure fair treatment of women-, veteran-, LGBTQ- and minority-owned businesses.
Will review agency contracting against the 25-point inclusion standard adopted by Massport.
Will audit state programs designed to assist minority businesses, including how quickly and equitably they are certified.
Will report on gender and racial pay disparities within state government.

in-sos-2026-engling-max.name: Max Engling
in-sos-2026-engling-max.bio: Former U.S. Senate staffer and U.S. House Administration Committee staffer; worked at Beck's Hybrids.

positions.stance: Will ensure only U.S. citizens vote in Indiana elections and protect the integrity of the voter rolls.
Proposes a direct channel for citizens to report potential election issues themselves.
Will screen business filings to push back on shell companies that register identical LLCs to defraud customers or avoid regulation.
Will "slash onerous regulations on small businesses and streamline business services."

in-sos-2026-bayh-beau.name: Beau Bayh
in-sos-2026-bayh-beau.bio: U.S. Marine Corps infantry officer who rose to the rank of Captain.

positions.stance: First priority is cleaning up corruption and wasteful spending in the Secretary of State's office.
"No illegal votes – period – but every legal Hoosier's vote should count"; will strengthen election security and participation.
Supports statewide ballot referendums letting voters weigh in on issues including redistricting.
Will advocate for small businesses and cut red tape and wasteful spending.
Will fight excessive taxes on working people, support labor unions, and work to rebuild a strong middle class.

in-comptroller-2026-nieshalla-elise.name: Elise Nieshalla
in-comptroller-2026-nieshalla-elise.bio: Indiana State Comptroller since 2023, with experience in business, local government and real estate investment.

positions.stance: Supports President Trump's America First agenda and will fight for free enterprise and the rights to life, self-defense and religious liberty.
Champions policies that strengthen Indiana's financial position, including low debt, balanced budgets, healthy reserves and well-funded pensions.
Leads state financial officers urging national leaders to spend less, create a path to a balanced budget, and reduce the debt.
Works to remove state retirement assets from funds tied to the Chinese Communist Party or focused on ESG factors.
Works to enhance operations "without growing government" and is adding federal grant data to the Indiana Transparency Portal.

in-comptroller-2026-bailey-jessica.name: Jessica Bailey
in-comptroller-2026-bailey-jessica.bio: Porter County Clerk for two terms.

positions.stance: Will make the state transparency portal easier to search, in plain language, and kept current so Hoosiers can see how tax money is spent.
Will be an independent voice on the State Board of Finance: "No money should move without an independent set of eyes on it."
Will bring her county standard statewide: "every dollar accounted for, every payment on time."
Will ensure state funds to local governments and schools are tracked clearly, handled responsibly and paid on time.

in-treas-2026-elliott-daniel.name: Daniel Elliott
in-treas-2026-elliott-daniel.bio: Indiana State Treasurer since 2022; former Morgan County Councilman and owner of a software company.

in-treas-2026-kebe-coumba.name: Coumba Kebe
in-treas-2026-kebe-coumba.bio: Background in public health and healthcare operations and advocacy.

positions.stance: Will make state financial information easier to access and understand through plain-language reporting and modern communication tools.
Indiana should evaluate financial decisions on their long-term impact on workforce, communities, economic growth and quality of life.
Will prioritize outreach so more families can access Treasurer's Office programs to save, invest and plan for higher education.
Wants financial decisions viewed through the lens of their impact on Hoosier families, including childcare, healthcare and aging.

md-comp-2026-lierman-brooke.name: Brooke Elizabeth Lierman
md-comp-2026-lierman-brooke.bio: Comptroller of Maryland, civil rights attorney, and former eight-year State Delegate from Baltimore City.

positions.stance: Committed to building communities that are "more equitable, more resilient, and more prosperous" and to modernizing the office.
Committed to best value on every expenditure and using state dollars to close the racial wealth divide and build a climate-resilient state.
Will pursue proactive outreach and close the tax gap to fund priorities including public education and the clean energy transition.
Will move the Comptroller's office from mainframe systems to the cloud.

md-comp-2026-dunn-sonya.name: Sonya Dunn
md-comp-2026-dunn-sonya.bio: CEO and founder of JEMH Enterprises LLC and business executive.

positions.stance: The Comptroller's Office should serve as Maryland's "fiscal watchdog" protecting taxpayers and ensuring accountability.
Will work to fix problems in Maryland's public finances at the state, county and local levels.
Says Maryland deserves financial leadership that puts people first, not politics, special interests or bureaucracy.

md-ag-2026-brown-anthony.name: Anthony G. Brown
md-ag-2026-brown-anthony.bio: Maryland Attorney General; former Lieutenant Governor, member of Congress, state legislator and U.S. Army veteran.

md-ag-2026-rutledge-james.name: James B. Rutledge, III
md-ag-2026-rutledge-james.bio: Maryland attorney with decades of law practice.

positions.stance: Will fight crime at every level "without playing politics with our communities or government officials."
Will combat hackers, cyber predators and scam artists who prey on the elderly and vulnerable.
Will protect clean water and the Chesapeake Bay.

mo-auditor-2026-fitzpatrick-scott.name: Scott Fitzpatrick
mo-auditor-2026-fitzpatrick-scott.bio: Missouri State Auditor and business owner; former State Treasurer and House Budget Committee chairman.

positions.stance: Where waste, fraud and abuse occur, "I will find it and root it out."
Will ensure tax dollars are not spent providing benefits to illegal immigrants.
Will give taxpayers the facts and fight for reforms where programs benefit insiders through sweetheart deals.
Will review school administrative costs and salaries and measure school performance against taxpayer investment.
Will lead a comprehensive audit of any local government failing to protect the taxpayers it serves.
